q: Which Harappan site in Gujarat is famous for the remains of an ancient dockyard?
e: Lothal, in Ahmedabad district near the Bhogavo river, has a large brick basin identified as a dockyard.

q: The Harappan city of Dholavira is located on which island of the Rann of Kutch?
e: Dholavira lies on Khadir Bet in Kutch; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

q: Which archaeologist led the excavation of Lothal from 1955 onwards?
e: Lothal was excavated under S. R. Rao of the ASI; R. S. Bisht later excavated Dholavira.

q: Emperor Ashoka's major rock edicts in Gujarat are inscribed near which hill?
e: Ashoka's fourteen major rock edicts are carved on a boulder at the foot of Girnar near Junagadh.

q: The Sudarshan lake near Girnar was originally constructed during the reign of which ruler?
e: It was built by Pushyagupta, governor under Chandragupta Maurya; Rudradaman I and Skandagupta later had it repaired.

q: Valabhi was the capital of which dynasty that ruled Gujarat?
e: The Maitrakas, founded by Bhatarka, ruled from Valabhi, which was also a renowned centre of learning.

q: Who founded the city of Anhilwad Patan?
e: Vanraj Chavda of the Chavda dynasty founded Anhilwad Patan in the 8th century.

q: Rani ki Vav at Patan was built by Queen Udayamati in memory of which king?
e: Udayamati built the stepwell in memory of her husband, Solanki king Bhimdev I; it is a UNESCO site since 2014.

q: Mahmud of Ghazni raided the Somnath temple (1025-26 CE) during the reign of which Solanki king?
e: Bhimdev I was ruling at Anhilwad Patan when Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Somnath in 1025-26 CE.

q: Hemchandracharya composed the grammar 'Siddha-Hema-Shabdanushasana' under the patronage of which ruler?
e: The work was written at Siddhraj Jaysinh's request, and its title joins the names of the king (Siddha) and the author (Hema).

q: Which Solanki ruler embraced Jainism under the influence of Hemchandracharya and prohibited animal slaughter?
e: Kumarpal (12th century), successor of Siddhraj, became a follower of Jainism under Hemchandracharya.

q: Karnadev, popularly called 'Karan Ghelo', the last Rajput ruler of Gujarat, belonged to which dynasty?
e: Karnadev Vaghela lost Gujarat to Alauddin Khilji's army around 1299 CE.

q: Who founded the city of Ahmedabad in 1411?
e: Ahmed Shah I of the Gujarat Sultanate founded Ahmedabad on the banks of the Sabarmati in 1411.

q: Which Sultan of Gujarat captured Pavagadh in 1484 and made Champaner his capital?
e: Mahmud Begada conquered Champaner in 1484; Champaner-Pavagadh is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: Which Sultan of Gujarat was killed in 1537 during an encounter with the Portuguese off Diu?
e: Bahadur Shah died near Diu in 1537 while dealing with the Portuguese, who then strengthened their hold there.

q: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate his conquest of:
e: Akbar built the Buland Darwaza to mark his victorious Gujarat campaign of 1572-73.

q: Where was Mahatma Gandhi born?
e: Gandhiji was born at Porbandar on 2 October 1869.

q: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was born at which place?
e: Patel was born at Nadiad on 31 October 1875; Karamsad was his ancestral village.

q: Vallabhbhai Patel received the title 'Sardar' after leading which movement?
e: The women of Bardoli honoured him as 'Sardar' after the successful 1928 no-tax campaign.

q: During which 1918 movement in Gujarat did Gandhiji undertake his first fast in India?
e: In March 1918 Gandhiji fasted in support of Ahmedabad mill workers' demand for higher wages.

q: The Kheda Satyagraha of 1918 was mainly concerned with:
o: Remission of land revenue after crop failure
e: Kheda's peasants demanded suspension of revenue collection due to crop failure; Gandhiji and Patel led them.

q: Gandhiji's Dandi March of 1930 began from:
e: He set out from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.

q: Which was the first ashram set up by Gandhiji in India after his return from South Africa?
e: Gandhiji founded Kochrab Ashram in Ahmedabad in 1915 and moved to the Sabarmati site in 1917.

q: On which date did Gujarat come into existence as a separate state?
e: Gujarat was carved out of the bilingual Bombay State under the Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960.

q: Who led the Mahagujarat Movement and is affectionately called 'Indu Chacha'?
e: Indulal Yagnik led the Mahagujarat Janata Parishad, which campaigned for a separate Gujarat state.

q: Who formally inaugurated the new state of Gujarat on 1 May 1960?
e: The Gandhian social worker Ravishankar Maharaj inaugurated the state of Gujarat.

q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Gujarat?
e: Dr. Jivraj Mehta became Gujarat's first Chief Minister on 1 May 1960.

q: The 'Aarzi Hukumat' (provisional government) formed in 1947 against the Nawab of Junagadh was headed by:
e: Samaldas Gandhi headed the Aarzi Hukumat, whose campaign helped bring Junagadh into the Indian Union.

q: Shyamji Krishna Varma, founder of India House in London, was born in which town?
e: Shyamji Krishna Varma was born at Mandvi in Kutch in 1857 and founded India House in 1905.

q: Gujarat Vidyapith in Ahmedabad was founded in 1920 by:
e: Gandhiji founded Gujarat Vidyapith as a national university during the Non-Cooperation Movement.
